power.model: Idealised direct-beam incidence: factor = visible solar-disk fraction × max(0, cos θ), θ = angle between the Sun direction and the panel normal. Ignores cell efficiency, temperature, degradation, dust, wiring and pointing losses, so it is an upper bound, not electrical output.

site_context.coordinate_source: Local summit (4993 m) found in the Moon Trek 30 m LOLA DEM within 4 km of the commonly quoted Malapert Mountain point (-85.99, 357.07). That point sits on the flank: a ridge 100 m north blocks Earth 100% of the time; the summit sees Earth 99.9%.

notes: Real data = Sun/Earth azimuth-elevation from JPL Horizons and terrain horizons from Moon Trek LOLA DEMs, precomputed by the data engine (data/sites/). Statistics are hourly samples over the mission.

Sunlit = any part of the solar disk above the local terrain horizon. Earth visible = Earth's centre above the terrain horizon. This is geometric line of sight only; it does not guarantee a working radio link (antenna pointing, ground-station schedules and link budget are not modelled).
Viability (pass/fail, score, violations) comes from the team's viability evaluator; the comparison system only displays and sorts it.
